lab_abnormal: the template lab_abnormal

Source: R/tpl_docs.R
tfl_tpl_lab_abnormal.Rd

The table template lab_abnormal, layout summary. Its program is one call, tfl_tpl(ard, "lab_abnormal", ...); a parameter a report leaves out takes the study standard's value, else the variant's default, else the layout's.

Parameters

ParameterTierStageDefaultMaps toWhat
populationrequiredcalloutput.populationthe analysis set's id (SAF)
subsetothercallwhich subjects (R, on the analysis set's ADSL): PART == "Part 1"
dataothercallADLBthe dataset of records
paramsothercallthe PARAMCD values; NULL: all
whereothercallthe records kept (R), e.g. ONTRTFL == "Y"
byothercallTRT01Asettings.treatmentthe column variable
param_orderothercallPARAMNthe parameters' order variable; NULL: by name
categoryothercallANRINDthe category's variable (ANRIND, a criterion's MCRIT1ML)
levelsothercallthe values counted, in order (lowest first); NULL: the code list's
cumulativeothercallFALSEcount a subject in every level up to their worst (level 2 or more ...)
baseline_normalothercallFALSEonly the subjects normal at baseline, in n and in the N
baselineothercallBNRINDthe category at baseline
baseline_valueothercallNORMALthe value of 'baseline' that is normal
data_idothercallthe analysis data's id; NULL: _
headingothercallParameter / Categorythe label column's heading

Aliases

The same template by the names of other collections' items: each runs it as itself (tfl_tpl(x, "stf_t20_kidney_level", ...)).

AliasCollectionItemTitle
stf_t20_kidney_levelFDA STF IG v2T20Kidney function values above levels
stf_t36_sbp_maxFDA STF IG v2T36Maximum postbaseline systolic BP categories
stf_t37_dbp_maxFDA STF IG v2T37Maximum postbaseline diastolic BP categories
stf_t38_hypotensionFDA STF IG v2T38Postbaseline hypotension criteria
stf_t52_chem_last_l2FDA STF IG v2T52Last on-treatment chemistry at level 2 or above
stf_t53_hem_last_l2FDA STF IG v2T53Last on-treatment hematology at level 2 or above
phuse_os_abnormalPhUSE CSSOS table abnormalPostbaseline values outside normal range

A U.S. Government work; FDA's website content is in the public domain unless noted (https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/about-website/website-policies).

  • PhUSE CSS: PhUSE CSS Development of Standard Scripts for Analysis and Programming Working Group. Analyses and Displays Associated with Measures of Central Tendency: Focus on Vital Sign, Electrocardiogram, and Laboratory Analyte Measurements in Phase 2-4 Clinical Trials and Integrated Submission Documents (white paper), Version 1.0, 10 October 2013. https://github.com/phuse-org/phuse-scripts/tree/master/whitepapers (accessed 2026-10-28). Analyses and Displays Associated with Outliers or Shifts from Normal to Abnormal: Focus on Vital Signs, Electrocardiogram, and Laboratory Analyte Measurements in Phase 2-4 Clinical Trials and Integrated Summary Documents (white paper), Version 1.0, 10 September 2015. https://github.com/phuse-org/phuse-scripts/tree/master/whitepapers (accessed 2026-10-28). Copyright PHUSE Limited, all rights reserved; cited by number only.

  • PhUSE CSS: PhUSE CSS Standard Analyses Working Group. Analysis and Displays Associated with Adverse Events: Focus on Adverse Events in Phase 2-4 Clinical Trials and Integrated Summary Documents (white paper), Version 1.0, 3 February 2017. https://phuse.global/Deliverables (accessed 2026-10-28). Copyright PHUSE Limited, all rights reserved; cited by number only.

  • PhUSE CSS: PhUSE CSS Standard Analyses Working Group. Analyses and Displays Associated with Demographics, Disposition, and Medications in Phase 2-4 Clinical Trials and Integrated Summary Documents (white paper), Version 2.0, 2 March 2018. https://phuse.global/Deliverables (accessed 2026-10-28). Copyright PHUSE Limited, all rights reserved; cited by number only.

The aliases follow the numbering of these publications, and the titles are short descriptions of our own, not their text. The templates are tflspec's, not endorsed or recommended by FDA or PhUSE.

Example

plan <- tfl_tpl(ard, "lab_abnormal", population = "SAF", levels = c("LOW", "HIGH"), where = "ONTRTFL == \"Y\"")

See also

tfl_tpl(), tfl_tpl_help(), tfl_tpl_args(), tfl_templates()

tfl_tpl_help("lab_abnormal", tier = c("required", "usual"))

#>   population | - (template)      | the analysis set's id (SAF)
